name: apps
title: Applications
description: Installed applications with their own icons: .app bundles on macOS (running ones tagged, with Quit and Hide; the System Settings panes as rows), .desktop entries on Linux (their own actions as secondary actions).
author: pal

settings.label: Extra folders
settings.description: Scanned in addition to the system's application folders.

store.tagline: Every installed app, with its icon, a keystroke from launch
features: macOS: `.app` bundles in `/Applications`, `/System/Applications` and `~/Applications`, one level deep so the Utilities folders come along
Linux: `.desktop` entries from every XDG data dir and the flatpak exports, hidden and `NoDisplay` ones skipped
The bundle id and the display name are keywords, so `com.apple.` or `Chrome` finds the app
A running app carries a green `Running` tag and gains Quit (`cmd+q`) and Hide (`cmd+h`)
35 System Settings panes as rows on macOS: `Keyboard`, `Displays`, `Privacy & Security`, found by words like `dark mode` or `dns`
A `.desktop` file's own actions (`New Private Window`) are the row's secondary actions on Linux
`cmd+i` shows the path, bundle id, version and whether it runs

screenshots.caption: The applications, their source as the subtitle, the running ones tagged
Typing at the root: the name, the bundle id and the display name all match
A running app: Open, Quit, Hide, Reveal in Finder, Copy path, Copy bundle id
The System Settings panes are rows too, found by what they hold
